We are looking for TWO QA Engineer Interns to join us this summer☀️.




Please note this is a fixed term position - starting 16 November 2026 and finishing 12 February 2027.




About the role:

Are you a recent graduate or final-year student passionate about software quality and automation? Join our team as a QA Engineer Intern and gain hands-on experience in building and running automated tests that help ensure the reliability of our software systems. 

This internship is designed to help you apply what you've learned in university to real-world engineering challenges, with mentorship from experienced professionals. 




To be eligible for this role you must:

Have completed study (within the last 12 months) or be currently studying Computer Science or Software Engineering

Be studying at NZQA qualification level 6-10

Have not previously been employed by Calderwood in a FT position

Have not undertaken more than 2 pervious internships at Calderwood




The pay rate for this role is $29.90 per hour for the duration of the internship.




What will you be doing:

Learn how to write and run automated tests for web and desktop applications. 

Work with engineers and testers to understand how software is built and validated. 

Help identify areas where automation can improve testing efficiency. 

Use tools like Playwright and Leapwork to build test scripts. 

Participate in team meetings and Agile development processes. 

Document your work and share your learnings with the team. 

How to use AI to assist in the creation of Test Plans and scripts 




Tools & Technologies You'll Be Exposed To

Languages: C#, Typescript/JavaScript, or Python (basic knowledge is enough) 

Tools: Playwright, Leapwork, Copilot 

Platforms: Windows (WPF), Web 

Development Environment: Visual Studio Code, Git & GitHub, Azure DevOps 




What can you bring to this role:

Currently studying or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field. 

Familiarity with programming concepts and basic coding skills. 

Interest in software testing and quality assurance. 

Willingness to learn new tools and technologies. 

Good communication and teamwork skills. 

Able to work independently & within a team.




What You’ll Learn 

How automated testing fits into the software development lifecycle. 

Best practices for writing maintainable and effective test scripts. 

How to collaborate in a professional engineering team. 

Exposure to Agile methodologies and CI/CD pipelines. 




Bonus Points (Not Required) 

You’ve done a university project involving automated testing. 

You’ve explored tools like Playwright or similar automation frameworks tools or written basic test scripts. 

You’re curious about how large-scale software systems are tested. 




Join the A today!

We welcome candidates who are eligible to work in Auckland, New Zealand. This is an in-office role. 

No visa sponsorship available for this role. 

We foster a culture of belonging, empowerment, and growth for all. If you require any specific support or adjustments throughout the recruitment process to enable you to put your best foot forward, please don’t hesitate to let us know. 

A background check and skills assessment form part of our recruitment process.

Please note that we do not accept applications from recruiters or agencies for this position.
